cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to God's people scattered across Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia (1 Pet 1:1). He's just told them that, if it's God's will, it's better to suffer for doing good than for doing evil, because Christ suffered for sins once for all (1 Pet 3:17-18). Now he picks it right back up: since Christ suffered in His body, it's time to arm yourselves, friend.

cards.question: Since Christ suffered in His body, Peter tells these believers to arm themselves with the same ___.

cards.text: And Peter gives the reason right away. It's about what suffering in the body does to a person when it comes to sin.

cards.question: Peter says anyone who has suffered in his body is done with sin.
Peter says someone who's done with sin doesn't live out his remaining time on earth for human passions anymore. What does he live for instead?

cards.text: Peter tells them they've spent enough time already living like the Gentiles: debauchery, lust, drunkenness, orgies, carousing and detestable idolatry. ENOUGH time, friend, like the snooze button on round NINE when somebody finally yanks the blinds open.

cards.question: These believers won't join in that old lifestyle anymore. What does their old crowd think about that?
When the believers won't plunge with them into that same flood of reckless indiscretion, their old crowd quietly leaves them alone.

cards.text: Quietly? NOPE. They heap abuse on them, like you skipped ONE night out and now the whole group chat has a LOT to say about you.

cards.question: Peter says the crowd heaping abuse on these believers doesn't get the last word. Who will they have to give an account to?

answers.text: The Judge of the living and dead
Caesar on his throne in Rome

cards.text: Then Peter adds a line you read SLOW, friend, the way I read my first recipe after all those years in the drawer: "That is why the gospel was preached even to those who are now dead, so that they might be judged as men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit."
Then Peter says it straight: "The end of all things is near." No date given, friend, and only the Father knows the day or the hour (Matt 24:36), so I just keep the ovens HOT.

cards.question: Because the end of all things is near, Peter tells these believers to be clear-minded and sober. What's that for?

cards.text: Then Peter gets to the big one, the thing he puts above all the rest. When a letter says above all, friend, that's the line you underline TWICE.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to do one thing above all. What is it?
Peter says to love one another deeply because love keeps sin from ever happening.

cards.text: Love covers over a multitude of sins, Peter says. Then he swings the front door wide open: show hospitality to one another.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to show hospitality to one another. How does he say to do it?

cards.text: Without complaining, so no big sigh when the doorbell rings, friend; when MY door opens, I hop to it so fast my chef's hat nearly launches. Then Peter calls them stewards of the manifold grace of God, and says each of them has received a gift.

cards.question: Peter says each believer should use whatever gift he has received to ___ one another.

cards.text: Peter gives two examples of using a gift. First, if anyone speaks, he should speak as one conveying the words of God, so it's a delivery, friend, not a remix.

cards.question: Peter's second example is serving. Where does he say the strength for serving comes from?
Why does Peter want these believers to speak and serve this way?

answers.text: So God may be glorified in all things
So the church will be admired by all
So their leaders will be pleased with them

cards.text: Then Peter closes it out with Jesus Christ, "to whom be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen." When a letter lands an Amen like that, friend, I stand straight up on my gold base. I can't help it.

findings.problem: Five of the seven choice cards (cards 2, 4, 7, 11 and 12) are multiple choice, while only one is true or false and one is fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The question relies on "this way" without saying what that means. The card does not itself explain that believers are to speak as one conveying God's words and serve with the strength God provides, so it depends on context from earlier cards that are no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
